subject: Post-call: TCO squeeze & prioritized levers for NorthGate PoV
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Hwang <lisa.hwang@northgate.ai>, procurement@northgate.ai
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-04T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: TCO squeeze & prioritized levers for NorthGate PoV

Hi Lisa — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call and explicit next steps so we can align with your procurement/CFO needs. I condensed the levers we discussed and the asks you flagged. Attachments: northgate_tco_presentation.pdf (slides), NorthGate-MA-forecast.xlsx (per-scenario token run rates).

Summary of pain / constraints you emphasized:
- Production latency needs (~<200ms P50 for single-turn classification).
- Budget ceiling for initial PoV ~ $10k–$18k/month (you mentioned internal target at the low end).
- Procurement gate: 6-month limited PoV preferred before multi-year commitment; CFO wants a hard monthly cap.

Goals we agreed to measure in the PoV:
- 90%+ accuracy vs current heuristic for intent classification (sample eval will be provided).
- Throughput target: 75k inference calls/day (peak pattern: bursty mornings).
- Cost metric: cost per 1k requests and end-to-end token unit economics for your conversational flows.

Prioritized cost/TCO levers we recommend (in order):
1) Batching + micro-batching policy: expected 20–35% token cost reduction for your traffic shape (we tested similar SaaS customers).
2) Prefix KV caching for common prompts (30–50% saving for repeat flows in your dataset).
3) Model variant + quantization: smaller quantized variant for lower-latency routing (10–25% unit savings, slightly lower quality on fringe cases).
4) Routing fallback policy: route non-critical requests to lower-cost model during peak.

Preliminary economics (see attached spreadsheet for full math):
- Conservative PoV estimate (including infra, model variants, monitoring): $14,000/month for 75k calls/day baseline with moderate caching (assumes 1.8 tokens/request avg in generation step).
- Optimistic (aggressive batching & KV cache): $9,500/month.

Asks / next steps (action owners):
- Lisa / Procurement: confirm internal monthly cap and target decision date (Procurement contact listed in cc). (Action: procurement@northgate.ai)
- NorthGate Product: share a 2k-sample of representative request logs (anonymized) so we can size batching / cache gains. (Action: Lisa)
- Redwood (Marcus / Grace): produce a 6-week PoV plan with a SOW, acceptance criteria, and success metrics; include a capped pricing option and an aggressive optimization milestone at week 4. (Action: Marcus)
- Legal / Contracts (Aditya): prepare a short-form PoV SOW with limited liability and defined exit. (Action: Aditya; I’ve cc'd Aditya to accelerate.)

If you want, we can propose two PoV options in the SOW: (A) fixed monthly cap + performance gates, (B) usage + hard ceiling with auto-throttle. We recommend (B) if the CFO needs firm cost control.

Please reply with the single-number monthly cap your finance team would accept for an initial 6-month PoV and attach the anonymized request sample when convenient. I’ll follow up with a draft SOW and the detailed forecast by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks again,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Attachments: northgate_tco_presentation.pdf (18 slides) — high-level TCO scenarios; NorthGate-MA-forecast.xlsx (3 scenarios)
From: Lisa Hwang <lisa.hwang@northgate.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@northgate.ai, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@northgate.ai>
Date: 2027-12-04T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: TCO squeeze & prioritized levers for NorthGate PoV

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the crisp recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Our initial internal cap for a PoV we can reasonably get approved is $12k/month (we can stretch to $15k with executive signoff, but CFO prefers a hard cap).
- We will send an anonymized 2k-sample of request logs by end of week (engineering busy but will prioritize).
- Procurement asked whether you can do a 6-week milestone at week 4 for measurable cost improvements before the monthly cap moves. If you include an aggressive optimization milestone, Procurement is much more comfortable.

Looping Rajiv (CFO) and procurement for visibility — they’ll confirm the cap.

On the per-1k request estimate: can you include both a P50 and P95 cost line (post-batching + cache) in the SOW so our finance team can model variability?

Lisa
Lisa Hwang
Head of Product | NorthGate AI

Marcus / Aditya — quick engineering-backed numbers and suggested SOW structure: attaching redwood_pov_sow-draft.docx (stub) and I've updated the forecast with a conservative fallback column in the attached XLSX.

Engineering assumptions (conservative):
- Avg tokens/request (inference + prompt) = 3.2 tokens per call (we used a safety factor vs your sample to account for variability).
- Batching gain conservatively estimated at 18% (with queue latency constraint at P50 < 200ms).
- KV cache hit assumptions: 22% hit rate in PoV (we will instrument and report actual hit rate).

Conservative PoV monthly cost (SOW baseline): $13,800 (includes monitoring, model hosting, 2 model variants, and 24/7 incident paging).
Optimistic baseline after week-4 optimization: $10,200/month (target with aggressive batching + cache tuning).

SOW structure we propose:
- PoV term: 6 months with a 30-day cancel clause.
- Acceptance criteria at week 6: accuracy & latency gates + documented 10–20% cost reduction vs baseline.
- Week-4 optimization milestone with documented deliverables and a 10% rebate if milestone not met.
- Data controls: data residency/retention settings + audit logs (we will include minimal config for your security team).

I added a short drive link to the SOW draft for internal redlined iteration: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3RedwoodTCO

Aditya — can you take the SOW draft and produce a short-form PoV SOW we can send to Procurement by EOD Monday?

Thanks — will stand by to refine numbers once we get the sample.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pov_sow-draft.docx (SOW stub), NorthGate-MA-forecast.xlsx (updated conservative column)

Marcus — thanks for the follow-up. Forwarding with a couple of CFO-level asks so procurement can get a clean SOW. Quoting the last notes from Lisa below.

High-level CFO asks: 
1) We will approve a 6-month PoV at a hard cap of $12,000/month unless there is a materially stronger guarantee on cost reduction at month-2. (This is our preferred path.)
2) Define a clear SLAs/guardrails for throttling and cost overrun — we need an automatic throttle/stop if monthly spend approaches 90% of cap.
3) Provide a short PO or SOW template we can sign quickly; Procurement needs contractual language around data handling and liability limits.

If Redwood can accept the $12k cap for an initial 6-month PoV with: (a) week-4 optimization milestone and (b) automatic spend throttle at 90% of cap, we can move fast. Please send an updated short-form SOW reflecting these conditions and a one-page pricing sheet (P50/P95 lines as Lisa asked).

Rajiv
